## Purpose and research design

This notebook contains the standalone directional strategies, including their full process and optimization.
It starts from importing the futures and T-bill data, rebuilds the annual expanding-window
Schwartz--Smith (2000) model, evaluates the pre-specified one-contract
baselines, performs the calibration-only searches, freezes the resulting
rules, and reports the final risk-sized evidence.

The notebook starts from the raw weekly futures and T-bill files and rebuilds
the same annual expanding-window SS2000 filter used throughout the rest of the thesis.
The initial estimation window is 1990--1999, trading begins in 2000, parameters
are re-estimated at each calendar-year boundary, and only filtered states are
used. The 2000--2016 period is reported as calibration/development and
2017--2025 as the out-of-sample evidence.

The analysis distinguishes two economically different hypotheses:

1. **Short-Term-Deviation Contrarian Strategy:** short when the filtered
   short-term deviation is positive and long when it is negative.
2. **One-Week Model-Forecast Strategy:** hold the sign of the complete SS2000
   one-week-ahead log-price forecast change for the actual traded contract.

The calibration section calibrates the contrarian rule on CL1 only and applies
that frozen rule unchanged to CL2 and CL3 as maturity robustness checks. The
model-forecast rule is calibrated separately for CL1, CL5, CL9, CL13 and CL17;
all five maturity-specific results are reported, with no ex-post maturity
winner selected.
Selection uses 2000--2016 only. The 2017--2025 period is evaluated only after
each rule is frozen and is labelled retrospective OOS. All execution uses the
same underlying-contract roll logic and margin-account conventions as the
relative-value strategy, with maturity-specific outright margin requirements.


## Step 0: Computational Setup and Helper Functions
This section loads the required packages, defines raw-data and output paths,
and reproduces the SS2000 estimation and underlying-contract execution. 

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

set.seed(42)

#############################################################################
# STEP 0.1 — Packages
#############################################################################

library(tidyverse)   # core data stack
library(lubridate)   # date arithmetic (ymd, as.Date, etc.)
library(FKF)         # Fast Kalman Filter; state-space model estimation
library(readxl)      # read_xlsx; for loading DTB3 T-bill data
library(scales)      # readable axis and table labels

#############################################################################
# STEP 0.2 — File paths
#############################################################################

# Find the project from the notebook location 
find_project_root <- function(start_path) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start_path, mustWork = TRUE)

  for (i in 0:10) { 
    primary_data <- file.path(candidate, "data", "CL_weekly_full_with_underlying_v2.rds")
    if (file.exists(primary_data)) return(candidate)

    nested_project <- file.path(candidate, "MA Code ", "Master Thesis 1.1")
    nested_primary <- file.path(nested_project, "data", "CL_weekly_full_with_underlying_v2.rds")
    if (file.exists(nested_primary)) {
      return(normalizePath(nested_project, mustWork = TRUE))
    }

    parent <- dirname(candidate) 
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) break
    candidate <- parent
  }

  stop("Could not locate the Master Thesis 1.1 project folder from: ", start_path)
}

# During knitting, current_input() points to this R Markdown file. 
input_file <- tryCatch(
  knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE),
  error = function(e) character(0)
)
has_input_file <- length(input_file) == 1L &&
  !is.na(input_file) &&
  nzchar(input_file)

start_path <- if (has_input_file) dirname(input_file) else getwd()
DATA_ROOT <- find_project_root(start_path)

# Input: Bloomberg futures data (same .rds file used in the estimation code)
PATH_FUTURES <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "data", "CL_weekly_full_with_underlying_v2.rds")
if (!file.exists(PATH_FUTURES)) {
  stop("Authoritative futures file not found: ", PATH_FUTURES)
}

# Input: FRED 3-month T-bill rate (DTB3), weekly, ending Friday
PATH_TBILL <- file.path(DATA_ROOT, "data", "DTB3.xlsx")

# Output: every table and data object created by this notebook stays beside it.
# When code is run interactively, rebuild the notebook path from DATA_ROOT.
NOTEBOOK_DIR <- if (has_input_file) {

} else {

}
PATH_OUTPUT <- file.path(NOTEBOOK_DIR, "results")
dir.create(PATH_OUTPUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

#############################################################################
# STEP 0.3 — Strategy constants
#
# All key design parameters are defined in one place here.
#############################################################################

# Contracts used in the Kalman filter measurement equation (identical to
# the estimation code; all five are used for state extraction)
CONTRACTS <- c("CL1 Comdty", "CL5 Comdty", "CL9 Comdty", "CL13 Comdty", "CL17 Comdty")

# Row identifiers within the five-contract estimation panel.
IDX_CL1  <- 1L
IDX_CL17 <- 5L

# Weekly time step in year units (exact, consistent with estimation code)
DELTA_T <- 7 / 365.25

# Sample boundaries
TRAIN_START  <- as.Date("1990-01-05")   # first week included in any training window
FIRST_TRADE  <- as.Date("2000-01-01")   # first week of out-of-sample trading
                                         # (training block 1 = 1990-01-05 to 1999-12-31)

# Multi-start count for MLE optimisation 
N_STARTS <- 8L

# Development flag: set to TRUE to run a short test window only.
# Set to FALSE to run the full sample through 2025.
# When DEV_MODE = TRUE the strategy runs the 10Y-init setup through DEV_END only.
DEV_MODE <- FALSE
DEV_END  <- as.Date("2003-12-26")


#############################################################################
# STEP 0.4 — Custom print method for theta_hat objects
#
# Same as S&S 2000 Full Timeline.
#############################################################################

print.theta_hat <- function(x, ...) {
  y <- x
  if ("sigma_obs_raw" %in% names(y)) y$sigma_obs_raw <- NULL
  old_class <- class(y)
  class(y) <- setdiff(old_class, "theta_hat")
  print(y, ...)
  invisible(x)
}

#############################################################################
# STEP 0.4b — Execution helper functions
#
# These helpers support the explicit underlying-contract execution layer.
# Signals are defined for generic maturity ranks, while P&L and transaction
# costs are computed on the actual underlying futures ticker held through each
# weekly interval.
#############################################################################

generic_rank_from_name <- function(x) {
  as.integer(stringr::str_match(x, "^CL(\\d+) Comdty")[, 2])
}

sort_generic_cols <- function(cols) {
  cols[order(generic_rank_from_name(cols))]
}

match_ticker_index <- function(und_row, ticker) {
  idx <- which(!is.na(und_row) & und_row == ticker)
  if (length(idx) == 0L) NA_integer_ else idx[1L]
}

lookup_ticker_price <- function(px_row, und_row, ticker) {
  idx <- match_ticker_index(und_row, ticker)
  if (is.na(idx)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(px_row[idx])
}

lookup_ticker_ltd <- function(ltd_row, und_row, ticker) {
  idx <- match_ticker_index(und_row, ticker)
  if (is.na(idx)) return(as.Date(NA))
  val <- ltd_row[idx]
  if (inherits(val, "Date")) return(as.Date(val))
  if (is.numeric(val)) return(as.Date(val, origin = "1970-01-01"))
  as.Date(as.character(val))
}

next_ticker_in_ladder <- function(und_row, ticker) {
  idx <- match_ticker_index(und_row, ticker)
  if (is.na(idx)) return(NA_character_)
  later_idx <- which(!is.na(und_row) & seq_along(und_row) > idx)
  if (length(later_idx) == 0L) NA_character_ else und_row[later_idx[1L]]
}

choose_execution_ticker <- function(held_ticker, generic_ticker_next,
                                    prev_und_row, prev_ltd_row, next_obs_date) {
  advance_if_unsafe <- function(ticker) {
    if (is.na(ticker) || ticker == "") return(NA_character_)
    current_ticker <- ticker
    visited <- character()

    repeat {
      if (current_ticker %in% visited) {
        stop("Unsafe execution ladder cycle detected for ticker ", ticker)
      }
      visited <- c(visited, current_ticker)

      if (is.na(match_ticker_index(prev_und_row, current_ticker))) {
        stop("Ticker ", current_ticker, " not found in prior-week execution ladder")
      }

      ticker_ltd <- lookup_ticker_ltd(prev_ltd_row, prev_und_row, current_ticker)
      ticker_unsafe <- !is.na(ticker_ltd) && ticker_ltd <= next_obs_date
      if (!ticker_unsafe) return(current_ticker)

      next_ticker <- next_ticker_in_ladder(prev_und_row, current_ticker)
      if (is.na(next_ticker) || next_ticker == "") {
        stop("No safe successor found in execution ladder for ticker ", current_ticker)
      }
      current_ticker <- next_ticker
    }
  }

  if (is.na(generic_ticker_next) || generic_ticker_next == "") {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  if (is.na(held_ticker) || held_ticker == "") {
    return(advance_if_unsafe(generic_ticker_next))
  }

  if (is.na(match_ticker_index(prev_und_row, held_ticker))) {
    stop("Carried ticker ", held_ticker, " not found in prior-week execution ladder")
  }

  held_ltd <- lookup_ticker_ltd(prev_ltd_row, prev_und_row, held_ticker)
  generic_switch <- held_ticker != generic_ticker_next
  ltd_unsafe <- !is.na(held_ltd) && held_ltd <= next_obs_date

  if (generic_switch) {
    return(advance_if_unsafe(generic_ticker_next))
  }

  if (ltd_unsafe) {
    next_ticker <- next_ticker_in_ladder(prev_und_row, held_ticker)
    if (!is.na(next_ticker) && next_ticker != "") {
      return(next_ticker)
    }
    return(generic_ticker_next)
  }

  held_ticker
}

#############################################################################
# STEP 0.5 — Model helper functions
#
# Same as S&S 2000 Full Timeline (Steps 2 and 3).
# These are the exact same functions used for estimation, ensuring that the
# state-space system constructed during the forward filter in the strategy
# is identical to what was used during training.
#############################################################################

# ── A(T): maturity-dependent constant term in log futures pricing equation ──
# Equation (9) / A(T) in Schwartz & Smith (2000).
A_fun <- function(T, kappa, mu_star, sigma_chi, sigma_xi, rho, lambda_chi) {
  var_lnS <- (sigma_chi^2 / (2 * kappa)) * (1 - exp(-2 * kappa * T)) +
    sigma_xi^2 * T +
    2 * rho * sigma_chi * sigma_xi * (1 - exp(-kappa * T)) / kappa
  mu_star * T - (1 - exp(-kappa * T)) * (lambda_chi / kappa) + 0.5 * var_lnS
}

# ── W(Δt): discretised process noise covariance for state transition ────────
process_W <- function(Delta_t, kappa, sigma_chi, sigma_xi, rho) {
  var_chi    <- (sigma_chi^2 / (2 * kappa)) * (1 - exp(-2 * kappa * Delta_t))
  var_xi     <- sigma_xi^2 * Delta_t
  cov_chi_xi <- rho * sigma_chi * sigma_xi * (1 - exp(-kappa * Delta_t)) / kappa
  matrix(c(var_chi, cov_chi_xi,
           cov_chi_xi, var_xi), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
}

# ── make_ss_arrays(): build all FKF-ready state-space arrays ────────────────
# Constructs Zt (measurement matrix), ct (measurement intercept), GGt
# (measurement noise), Tt (transition matrix), dt (state drift), HHt
# (state noise) for a given theta and Tau matrix.
make_ss_arrays <- function(theta, Tau, Delta_t) {
  T_len <- ncol(Tau)
  m     <- nrow(Tau)
  n     <- 2L          # states: (chi, xi)

  with(as.list(theta), {

    Ft <- array(0, dim = c(m, n, T_len))
    d  <- matrix(0, nrow = m, ncol = T_len)

    for (tt in seq_len(T_len)) {
      tau_t      <- Tau[, tt]
      Ft[, , tt] <- cbind(exp(-kappa * tau_t), rep(1, m))
      d[, tt]    <- A_fun(tau_t, kappa, mu_star, sigma_chi, sigma_xi, rho, lambda_chi)
    }

    V <- diag(sigma_obs_vec^2, m)

    Tt  <- array(0, dim = c(n, n, T_len))
    dt  <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = T_len)
    HHt <- array(0, dim = c(n, n, T_len))

    for (tt in seq_len(T_len)) {
      G_t <- matrix(c(exp(-kappa * Delta_t), 0,
                      0,                     1),
                    nrow = n, byrow = TRUE)
      c_t <- c(0, mu * Delta_t)
      W_t <- process_W(Delta_t, kappa, sigma_chi, sigma_xi, rho)
      Tt[, , tt]  <- G_t
      dt[, tt]    <- c_t
      HHt[, , tt] <- W_t
    }

    list(
      Zt  = Ft,
      ct  = d,
      HHt = HHt,
      GGt = array(V, dim = c(m, m, T_len)),
      Tt  = Tt,
      dt  = dt
    )
  })
}

# ── apply_missing_mask_fkf(): handle NAs in Y for FKF ───────────────────────
# Missing observations are neutralised by zeroing out their rows in Zt/ct
# and inflating their measurement variance to a large number so the filter
# ignores them. Placeholder value of 0 is written into y_tilde.
apply_missing_mask_fkf <- function(Y, ss, big_var = NULL, big_var_mult = 1e6) {
  m     <- dim(ss$Zt)[1]
  T_len <- ncol(Y)

  y_tilde <- Y
  y_tilde[is.na(y_tilde)] <- 0

  Zt_new  <- ss$Zt
  ct_new  <- ss$ct
  GGt_new <- ss$GGt

  I <- diag(1, m)

  if (is.null(big_var)) {
    Vdiag <- diag(ss$GGt[, , 1])
    Vmed  <- median(Vdiag[is.finite(Vdiag) & Vdiag > 0])
    if (!is.finite(Vmed)) Vmed <- 1.0
    big_var <- big_var_mult * Vmed
  }

  for (tt in seq_len(T_len)) {
    miss         <- is.na(Y[, tt])
    M            <- diag(as.numeric(!miss), m, m)
    Zt_new[, , tt] <- M %*% Zt_new[, , tt]
    ct_new[, tt]   <- M %*% ct_new[, tt]
    V_base         <- GGt_new[, , tt]
    GGt_new[, , tt] <- M %*% V_base %*% M + (I - M) * big_var
  }

  list(yt  = y_tilde, Zt  = Zt_new, ct  = ct_new,
       GGt = GGt_new, Tt  = ss$Tt,  dt  = ss$dt, HHt = ss$HHt)
}

# ── softplus(): smooth R → R+ transform for measurement error parameters ────
softplus <- function(x) log1p(exp(-abs(x))) + pmax(x, 0)

# ── pack(): map theta list → unconstrained optimizer vector ─────────────────
pack <- function(theta) c(
  log(theta$kappa),
  theta$mu,
  theta$mu_star,
  log(theta$sigma_chi),
  log(theta$sigma_xi),
  atanh(theta$rho),
  theta$lambda_chi,
  theta$sigma_obs_raw
)

# ── unpack(): map optimizer vector → theta list (natural scale) ──────────────
unpack <- function(p) {
  if (length(p) < 8L) stop("unpack(): parameter vector too short (need >= 8 elements).")
  sigma_obs_raw <- as.numeric(p[8:length(p)])
  eps_sd        <- 1e-8
  list(
    kappa         = exp(p[1]),
    mu            = p[2],
    mu_star       = p[3],
    sigma_chi     = exp(p[4]),
    sigma_xi      = exp(p[5]),
    rho           = tanh(p[6]),
    lambda_chi    = p[7],
    sigma_obs_raw = sigma_obs_raw,
    sigma_obs_vec = softplus(sigma_obs_raw) + eps_sd
  )
}

# ── sample_start(): randomised but economically plausible starting values ───
# Called N_STARTS times in the MLE routine; identical to estimation code.
sample_start <- function() {
  sigma_obs_raw0 <- rnorm(length(CONTRACTS), mean = 0.12, sd = 0.10)
  list(
    kappa         = runif(1, 0.5, 5),
    mu            = runif(1, -0.10, 0.10),
    mu_star       = runif(1, -0.10, 0.10),
    sigma_chi     = runif(1, 0.05, 0.5),
    sigma_xi      = runif(1, 0.05, 0.5),
    rho           = runif(1, -0.95, 0.95),
    lambda_chi    = runif(1, -1, 1),
    sigma_obs_raw = sigma_obs_raw0
  )
}

# ── compute_prior_from_first_L(): data-based Kalman prior ───────────────────
# Pools the first L measurement equations (after removing A(tau) intercepts)
# and estimates initial (chi0, xi0) by OLS. Falls back to a diffuse prior if
# there is insufficient early data — critical for the first training block.
compute_prior_from_first_L <- function(Zt, ct, yt, L = 6, inflate = 2.0, nugget = 1e-8) {
  L <- min(L, ncol(yt))
  stopifnot(L >= 2)

  X_stack <- NULL
  y_stack <- NULL

  for (t in seq_len(L)) {
    Ft_full <- Zt[, , t]
    dtvec   <- ct[, t]
    yvec    <- yt[, t]
    obs     <- rowSums(abs(Ft_full)) > 0
    if (sum(obs) < 2L) next
    Ft      <- Ft_full[obs, , drop = FALSE]
    yy      <- as.vector(yvec[obs] - dtvec[obs])
    X_stack <- rbind(X_stack, Ft)
    y_stack <- c(y_stack, yy)
  }

  if (is.null(X_stack) || length(y_stack) < 6L) {
    return(list(m0 = c(0, 0), P0 = diag(1e6, 2)))
  }

  fit <- lm.fit(x = X_stack, y = y_stack)
  m0  <- as.vector(fit$coefficients)

  if (any(!is.finite(m0))) {
    return(list(m0 = c(0, 0), P0 = diag(1e6, 2)))
  }

  n_obs   <- length(y_stack)
  p_dim   <- ncol(X_stack)
  rss     <- sum(fit$residuals^2)
  s2      <- rss / max(1, n_obs - p_dim)

  XtX_inv <- tryCatch(
    solve(crossprod(X_stack) + diag(nugget, p_dim)),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(XtX_inv) || any(!is.finite(XtX_inv))) {
    P0 <- diag(1e6, 2)
  } else {
    P0 <- inflate * (s2 * XtX_inv + diag(nugget, p_dim))
    if (any(!is.finite(P0)) || det(P0) <= 0) P0 <- diag(1e6, 2)
  }

  list(m0 = m0, P0 = P0)
}

# ── loglik(): negative log-likelihood for optim() ───────────────────────────
# Identical to the estimation code. Takes the packed optimizer vector p,
# builds the state-space system, applies the missing mask, initialises the
# prior, runs the Kalman filter, and returns the negative log-likelihood.
loglik <- function(p, Y, Tau, Delta_t) {
  theta  <- unpack(p)
  ss     <- make_ss_arrays(theta, Tau, Delta_t)
  if (any(!is.finite(ss$ct))) return(1e6)
  masked <- apply_missing_mask_fkf(Y, ss)
  L_use  <- max(4L, min(6L, ncol(Y)))
  prior  <- tryCatch(
    compute_prior_from_first_L(masked$Zt, masked$ct, masked$yt,
                               L = L_use, inflate = 2.0),
    error = function(e) list(m0 = c(0, 0), P0 = diag(1e6, 2))
  )
  kf <- tryCatch(
    fkf(a0  = prior$m0,  P0  = prior$P0,
        dt  = masked$dt, ct  = masked$ct,
        Tt  = masked$Tt, Zt  = masked$Zt,
        HHt = masked$HHt, GGt = masked$GGt,
        yt  = masked$yt),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(kf) || !is.finite(kf$logLik)) return(1e6)
  -kf$logLik
}

#############################################################################
# STEP 0.6 — Sanity check: verify all required functions exist
#############################################################################

required_fns <- c(
  "A_fun", "process_W", "make_ss_arrays", "apply_missing_mask_fkf",
  "softplus", "pack", "unpack", "sample_start",
  "compute_prior_from_first_L", "loglik"
)

setup_env <- environment()
missing_fns <- required_fns[
  !vapply(required_fns, function(fn) {
    exists(fn, envir = setup_env, mode = "function", inherits = TRUE)
  }, logical(1))
]

if (length(missing_fns) > 0L) {
  stop("Step 0 incomplete — the following functions are missing: ",
       paste(missing_fns, collapse = ", "))
} else {
  message("✓ Step 0 complete — all ", length(required_fns),
          " helper functions loaded successfully.")
  message("✓ Research constants set:")
  message("    Training start     : ", TRAIN_START)
  message("    First trade        : ", FIRST_TRADE)
  message("    DEV_MODE           : ", DEV_MODE,
          if (DEV_MODE) paste0(" (through ", DEV_END, ")") else "")
  message("    Estimation panel   : ", paste(CONTRACTS, collapse = ", "))
  message("    Execution          : one actual underlying contract per strategy")
}

```


## Step 1: Data Loading, Matrix Construction and Roll Flags
This section loads all data required for the strategy. The futures data
loading and matrix construction (Y, Tau, obs_dates) is identical to
the S&S 2000 Full Timeline code, using the same .rds file, same column
conventions, same CL1 edge-case fix, same NA masking logic. After
building those matrices the section adds three things the estimation
code did not need: a subsetting of all matrices to the 1990 training
start, construction of binary roll flags for CL1 and CL17, and loading
of the DTB3 T-bill rate aligned to obs_dates.

```{r step1, message=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.0 — Load Bloomberg futures data
#############################################################################

weekly_full <- readr::read_rds(PATH_FUTURES) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date = as.Date(date))

# Column name vectors for the 5-contract signal set (built from CONTRACTS)
needed_px  <- paste0(CONTRACTS, "__PX")
needed_und <- paste0(CONTRACTS, "__UND")
needed_ltd <- paste0(CONTRACTS, "__LTD")

# Full generic ladder used by the underlying-contract execution engine.
all_px_cols  <- sort_generic_cols(grep("__PX$",  names(weekly_full), value = TRUE))
all_und_cols <- sort_generic_cols(grep("__UND$", names(weekly_full), value = TRUE))
all_ltd_cols <- sort_generic_cols(grep("__LTD$", names(weekly_full), value = TRUE))

# Safety: verify all required columns exist
stopifnot(all(needed_px  %in% names(weekly_full)))
stopifnot(all(needed_ltd %in% names(weekly_full)))
stopifnot(all(needed_und %in% names(weekly_full)))
stopifnot(length(all_px_cols)  == length(all_und_cols))
stopifnot(length(all_px_cols)  == length(all_ltd_cols))

# Sort by date
weekly_win <- weekly_full %>%
  dplyr::arrange(date)

# Full price / UND / LTD ladders by date, required for explicit held-contract
# execution. Rows are dates; columns are generic maturity slots CL1...CL120.
PX_ALL_full <- weekly_win %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(all_px_cols)) %>%
  as.matrix()
storage.mode(PX_ALL_full) <- "double"

UND_ALL_full <- weekly_win %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(all_und_cols)) %>%
  as.matrix()

LTD_ALL_full <- weekly_win %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(all_ltd_cols)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.character)) %>%
  as.matrix()

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.1 — Build log-price observation matrix Y
# Rows = contracts (CL1, CL5, CL9, CL13, CL17), Cols = observation dates
#############################################################################

weekly_log <- weekly_win %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    obs_date = date,
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::all_of(needed_px),
      ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), NA_real_, log(as.numeric(.x))),
      .names = "log_{.col}"
    )
  )

Y_full <- weekly_log %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::starts_with("log_")) %>%
  as.matrix() %>%
  t()

storage.mode(Y_full) <- "double"

obs_dates_full <- weekly_log$obs_date
colnames(Y_full) <- as.character(obs_dates_full)

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.2 — Build time-to-maturity matrix Tau
# Tau_{i,t} = (LTD_{i,t} - obs_date_t) / 365.25
#############################################################################

LTD_df <- weekly_win %>%
  dplyr::select(date, dplyr::all_of(needed_ltd))

LTD_mat <- LTD_df %>%
  dplyr::select(-date) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), as.Date)) %>%
  as.matrix()

Tau_full <- matrix(NA_real_,
                   nrow = length(CONTRACTS),
                   ncol = length(obs_dates_full))
rownames(Tau_full) <- CONTRACTS
colnames(Tau_full) <- as.character(obs_dates_full)

for (j in seq_along(obs_dates_full)) {
  tdate   <- obs_dates_full[j]
  ltd_vec <- as.Date(LTD_mat[j, ])
  tau_vec <- as.numeric(ltd_vec - tdate) / 365.25
  tau_vec[is.na(ltd_vec) | tau_vec <= 0] <- NA_real_
  Tau_full[, j] <- tau_vec
}

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.3 — CL1 edge-case fix + NA cleanup
#############################################################################

# CL1 row indices (same in both Y and Tau; contracts are in the same order)
cl1_row_Y   <- which(rownames(Y_full)   == paste0("log_", CONTRACTS[IDX_CL1], "__PX"))
cl1_row_Tau <- IDX_CL1   # = 1

stopifnot(length(cl1_row_Y) == 1L)

# Weeks where CL1 is on or past its LTD; drop the observation, keep Tau = 0
bad_cl1 <- which(is.na(Tau_full[cl1_row_Tau, ]) | Tau_full[cl1_row_Tau, ] <= 0)
Y_full[cl1_row_Y, bad_cl1]      <- NA_real_
Tau_full[cl1_row_Tau, bad_cl1]  <- 0        # keep finite for make_ss_arrays()

# Propagate: wherever Tau is NA, Y must also be NA
Y_full[is.na(Tau_full)] <- NA_real_

# Replace all remaining NA in Tau with 0 (required by make_ss_arrays)
Tau_full[is.na(Tau_full)] <- 0

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.4 — Load and align DTB3 T-bill rate
#
# Source: FRED series DTB3, sheet "Weekly, Ending Friday"
# Rate is annualised percent (e.g. 5.25 = 5.25% p.a.), discount basis.
# We forward-fill any missing weeks (holiday gaps) then align to obs_dates_full.
#############################################################################

dtb3_raw <- readxl::read_xlsx(PATH_TBILL, sheet = "Weekly, Ending Friday") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    date  = as.Date(observation_date),
    dtb3  = as.numeric(DTB3)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(date)

# Forward-fill any NA rates (FRED occasionally has gaps on holiday weeks)
dtb3_raw <- dtb3_raw %>%
  tidyr::fill(dtb3, .direction = "down")

# Align to obs_dates_full via a left join; futures dates are the master
# For any futures date with no exact T-bill match, carry forward the
# most recent available rate (rolling join using dplyr + fill)
tbill_aligned <- dplyr::tibble(date = obs_dates_full) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(dtb3_raw, by = "date") %>%
  tidyr::fill(dtb3, .direction = "down")

dtb3_full <- tbill_aligned$dtb3   # length = length(obs_dates_full)

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.5 — Subset everything to TRAIN_START (1990-01-05)
#
# The full matrices go back to 1984 but CL17 has gaps before 1990.
# All strategy work uses only obs_dates >= TRAIN_START.
# We keep _full objects intact and create clean _strat objects for all steps.
#############################################################################

strat_idx <- which(obs_dates_full >= TRAIN_START)

obs_dates  <- obs_dates_full[strat_idx]          # master date vector from here on
Y          <- Y_full[,   strat_idx, drop = FALSE] # 5 x T_strat log-price matrix
Tau        <- Tau_full[, strat_idx, drop = FALSE] # 5 x T_strat maturity matrix
dtb3       <- dtb3_full[strat_idx]                # length T_strat T-bill rate
PX_ALL     <- PX_ALL_full[strat_idx,  , drop = FALSE]
UND_ALL    <- UND_ALL_full[strat_idx, , drop = FALSE]
LTD_ALL    <- LTD_ALL_full[strat_idx, , drop = FALSE]

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.6 — Sanity checks
#############################################################################

# 1. Dimension consistency
stopifnot(ncol(Y)   == length(obs_dates))
stopifnot(ncol(Tau) == length(obs_dates))
stopifnot(length(dtb3)      == length(obs_dates))
stopifnot(nrow(PX_ALL)      == length(obs_dates))
stopifnot(nrow(UND_ALL)     == length(obs_dates))
stopifnot(nrow(LTD_ALL)     == length(obs_dates))

# 2. Date range
stopifnot(min(obs_dates) >= TRAIN_START)

# 3. No non-finite values in Tau (make_ss_arrays requires this)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(Tau)))

# 4. T-bill rate: no NAs after forward-fill
n_tbill_na <- sum(is.na(dtb3))
if (n_tbill_na > 0L) {
  warning("DTB3 has ", n_tbill_na, " NAs after forward-fill — check date alignment.")
}

# 5. Weekly gap check on strategy subsample
dt_days <- as.numeric(diff(obs_dates))
gaps_ok <- all(dt_days == 7L)

#############################################################################
# STEP 1.7 — Confirmation messages
#############################################################################

message("✓ Step 1 complete")
message("  Strategy sample   : ", min(obs_dates), " → ", max(obs_dates))
message("  Total weeks       : ", length(obs_dates))
message("  Y dimensions      : ", nrow(Y), " contracts × ", ncol(Y), " weeks")
message("  Tau non-finite    : ", sum(!is.finite(Tau)), " (must be 0)")
message("  T-bill NAs        : ", n_tbill_na, " (must be 0)")
message("  DTB3 range        : ", round(min(dtb3, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
        "% – ", round(max(dtb3, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "%")
message("  Full ladder cols   : ", ncol(PX_ALL))
message("  All gaps = 7 days : ", gaps_ok)

```


## Step 2: Rebalancing Schedule
This section constructs the complete rebalancing schedule used in Step 5.
Rebalancing is anchored to calendar year
boundaries read directly from obs_dates, no hardcoded week counts. For
each block the schedule records the integer indices into obs_dates for
the training window end, the trading window start, and the trading
window end. DEV_MODE is applied here, truncating the schedule to DEV_END
before any estimation begins.

```{r step2, message=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

#############################################################################
# STEP 2.0 — Apply DEV_MODE truncation
#
# If DEV_MODE = TRUE, we restrict obs_dates (and all aligned vectors) to
# dates up to and including DEV_END. This does NOT reload any data,
# it simply shortens the working vectors that all downstream steps use.
# To switch to the full sample, set DEV_MODE <- FALSE in Step 0 and rerun.
#############################################################################

if (DEV_MODE) {
  dev_idx    <- which(obs_dates <= DEV_END)
  obs_dates  <- obs_dates[dev_idx]
  Y          <- Y[,    dev_idx, drop = FALSE]
  Tau        <- Tau[,  dev_idx, drop = FALSE]
  dtb3       <- dtb3[dev_idx]
  PX_ALL     <- PX_ALL[dev_idx,  , drop = FALSE]
  UND_ALL    <- UND_ALL[dev_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  LTD_ALL    <- LTD_ALL[dev_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  message("DEV_MODE = TRUE — sample truncated to ", min(obs_dates), " → ", max(obs_dates))
} else {
  message("DEV_MODE = FALSE — using full sample ", min(obs_dates), " → ", max(obs_dates))
}

#############################################################################
# STEP 2.1 — Identify trading years from obs_dates
#
# Trading years are all calendar years in obs_dates that are >= year(FIRST_TRADE).
# Each trading year t uses:
#   - Training window : all obs_dates from TRAIN_START through end of year t-1
#   - Trading window  : all obs_dates where year(obs_date) == t
#
# We derive everything from the actual dates in obs_dates, so missing weeks
# or irregular gaps never cause the schedule to drift.
#############################################################################

all_years      <- lubridate::year(obs_dates)
trading_years  <- sort(unique(all_years[obs_dates >= FIRST_TRADE]))

stopifnot(length(trading_years) >= 1L)

#############################################################################
# STEP 2.2 — Build the schedule data frame
#
# One row per trading year. All columns are integer indices into obs_dates
#
# Columns:
#   trading_year     : calendar year being traded (e.g. 2000)
#   train_start_idx  : first index of training window (always 1 = TRAIN_START)
#   train_end_idx    : last index where year < trading_year
#   trade_start_idx  : first index where year == trading_year
#   trade_end_idx    : last index where year == trading_year
#   n_train_weeks    : number of training observations
#   n_trade_weeks    : number of trading observations
#############################################################################

schedule <- purrr::map_dfr(trading_years, function(yr) {

  # Training window: TRAIN_START up to and including last week of year yr-1
  train_idx  <- which(all_years < yr)

  # Trading window: all weeks in calendar year yr
  trade_idx  <- which(all_years == yr)

  # Both must be non-empty, if not, this year cannot be traded
  if (length(train_idx) == 0L || length(trade_idx) == 0L) return(NULL)

  dplyr::tibble(
    trading_year    = yr,
    train_start_idx = min(train_idx),   # always index 1 (TRAIN_START), expanding window
    train_end_idx   = max(train_idx),   # last week before this trading year
    trade_start_idx = min(trade_idx),   # first week of this trading year
    trade_end_idx   = max(trade_idx),   # last week of this trading year
    n_train_weeks   = length(train_idx),
    n_trade_weeks   = length(trade_idx)
  )
})

stopifnot(nrow(schedule) >= 1L)

# Verify expanding window property: train_end_idx must strictly increase
stopifnot(all(diff(schedule$train_end_idx) > 0L))

# Verify no overlap between training and trading windows
stopifnot(all(schedule$train_end_idx < schedule$trade_start_idx))

# Verify contiguous trading windows (trade_end of year k+1 > trade_end of year k)
stopifnot(all(diff(schedule$trade_end_idx) > 0L))

#############################################################################
# STEP 2.3 — Confirmation messages
#############################################################################

message("✓ Step 2 complete — rebalancing schedule built")
message("  Trading years     : ", min(schedule$trading_year),
        " → ", max(schedule$trading_year),
        "  (", nrow(schedule), " blocks)")
message("  Training weeks    : ",
        min(schedule$n_train_weeks), " (block 1) → ",
        max(schedule$n_train_weeks), " (block ", nrow(schedule), ")")
message("  Trading weeks/yr  : ",
        min(schedule$n_trade_weeks), " – ",
        max(schedule$n_trade_weeks))
message("")
message("  Schedule preview:")

# Print the full schedule cleanly
print(
  schedule %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      train_start_date = obs_dates[train_start_idx],
      train_end_date   = obs_dates[train_end_idx],
      trade_start_date = obs_dates[trade_start_idx],
      trade_end_date   = obs_dates[trade_end_idx]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      trading_year,
      train_start_date, train_end_date, n_train_weeks,
      trade_start_date, trade_end_date, n_trade_weeks
    ),
  n = Inf
)

```


## Step 3: Parameter Estimation Function
This section wraps the MLE estimation logic into a single callable function
estimate_ss(). The function takes a training window subset of Y and Tau,
runs the multi-start BFGS optimisation, and returns the best theta_hat.
It is called once per rebalancing block in the outer loop (Step 7). The
estimation logic is identical to the S&S 2000 Full Timeline code; only the function
interface differs.

```{r step3, message=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

#############################################################################
# STEP 3.0 — estimate_ss(): MLE estimation for one training window
#
# Arguments:
#   Y_train   : 5 x n_train log-price matrix (subset of Y)
#   Tau_train : 5 x n_train maturity matrix (subset of Tau)
#   Delta_t   : weekly time step in years (= DELTA_T from Step 0)
#   n_starts  : number of random restarts for the optimiser (= N_STARTS)
#   block_id  : integer label for the block (used only in messages)
#
#############################################################################

estimate_ss <- function(Y_train, Tau_train, Delta_t, n_starts, block_id) {

  stopifnot(ncol(Y_train) == ncol(Tau_train))
  stopifnot(nrow(Y_train) == nrow(Tau_train))
  stopifnot(ncol(Y_train) >= 10L)   # need enough data to identify 2 factors

  message("  [Block ", block_id, "] Starting MLE — ",
          ncol(Y_train), " training weeks, ", n_starts, " restarts")

  # ── 1. Generate random starting vectors ───────────────────────────────────
  set.seed(42L + block_id)   # reproducible per block; different seed each block
  init_vecs <- replicate(n_starts, pack(sample_start()), simplify = FALSE)

  # ── 2. Run optimiser from each starting point ─────────────────────────────
  fits <- purrr::map(init_vecs, function(p0) {
    tryCatch(
      optim(
        par     = p0,
        fn      = loglik,
        Y       = Y_train,
        Tau     = Tau_train,
        Delta_t = Delta_t,
        method  = "BFGS",
        control = list(maxit = 4000L, reltol = 1e-10)
      ),
      error = function(e) list(value = Inf, par = p0, convergence = 99L)
    )
  })

  # ── 3. Remove degenerate runs ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  is_plausible <- function(fit) {
    if (!is.finite(fit$value) || fit$value >= 1e5) return(FALSE)
    th <- tryCatch(unpack(fit$par), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(th)) return(FALSE)
    th$kappa      > 0   && th$kappa      <= 50  &&
    th$sigma_chi  > 0   && th$sigma_chi  <=  5  &&
    th$sigma_xi   > 0   && th$sigma_xi   <=  5  &&
    abs(th$rho)   < 0.9999                       &&
    all(is.finite(th$sigma_obs_vec))             &&
    all(th$sigma_obs_vec > 0)
  }

  valid <- purrr::keep(fits, is_plausible)

  if (length(valid) == 0L) {
    message("  [Block ", block_id, "] WARNING: all ", n_starts,
            " runs degenerate, retrying with 16 tighter starts ...")
    set.seed(42L + block_id + 1000L)
    init_vecs_retry <- replicate(16L, pack(sample_start()), simplify = FALSE)
    fits_retry <- purrr::map(init_vecs_retry, function(p0) {
      tryCatch(
        optim(par = p0, fn = loglik, Y = Y_train, Tau = Tau_train,
              Delta_t = Delta_t, method = "BFGS",
              control = list(maxit = 4000L, reltol = 1e-10)),
        error = function(e) list(value = Inf, par = p0, convergence = 99L)
      )
    })
    valid <- purrr::keep(fits_retry, is_plausible)
    if (length(valid) == 0L) {
      stop("Block ", block_id, ": estimation failed after retry. ",
           "Check training data for this window.")
    }
  }

  # ── 4. Select the run with the highest log-likelihood ─────────────────────
  best <- valid[[which.min(purrr::map_dbl(valid, "value"))]]

  # ── 5. Unpack to natural scale and attach metadata ─────────────────────────
  theta_hat <- unpack(best$par)
  class(theta_hat) <- "theta_hat"

  theta_hat$loglik_converged  <- -best$value
  theta_hat$n_valid_runs      <- length(valid)
  theta_hat$lambda_xi_implied <- theta_hat$mu - theta_hat$mu_star

  # ── Extract final filtered state from training window ──────────────────────
  # Run one clean forward filter pass at the final theta_hat over the full
  # training window. The December posterior is retained for the boundary
  # signal, while FKF's one-step-ahead prediction becomes the prior for the
  # first January observation. This is fully look-ahead free (it only uses training data).
  ss_train   <- make_ss_arrays(theta_hat, Tau_train, Delta_t)
  masked_train <- apply_missing_mask_fkf(Y_train, ss_train)
  L_use      <- max(4L, min(6L, ncol(Y_train)))
  prior_train <- tryCatch(
    compute_prior_from_first_L(masked_train$Zt, masked_train$ct,
                               masked_train$yt, L = L_use, inflate = 2.0),
    error = function(e) list(m0 = c(0, 0), P0 = diag(1e6, 2))
  )
  kf_train <- tryCatch(
    fkf(a0  = prior_train$m0,  P0  = prior_train$P0,
        dt  = masked_train$dt, ct  = masked_train$ct,
        Tt  = masked_train$Tt, Zt  = masked_train$Zt,
        HHt = masked_train$HHt, GGt = masked_train$GGt,
        yt  = masked_train$yt),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (!is.null(kf_train) && all(is.finite(kf_train$att))) {
    n_train <- ncol(Y_train)
    theta_hat$att_train_end <- as.numeric(kf_train$att[,  n_train])
    theta_hat$Ptt_train_end <- kf_train$Ptt[,, n_train]
    theta_hat$at_trade_start <- as.numeric(kf_train$at[, n_train + 1L])
    theta_hat$Pt_trade_start <- kf_train$Pt[, , n_train + 1L]
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(theta_hat$at_trade_start)))
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(theta_hat$Pt_trade_start)))
    # Empirical SD of filtered chi over the entire training window.
    # Used in generate_signals() as the z-score normaliser (Option B).
    # Look-ahead free: computed entirely from training data.
    chi_train_vec           <- as.numeric(kf_train$att[1L, ])
    emp_sd                  <- sd(chi_train_vec, na.rm = TRUE)
    theta_hat$sigma_chi_emp <- if (is.finite(emp_sd) && emp_sd > 0) emp_sd else NA_real_
  } else {
    # Fallback to diffuse prior if filter fails (safty step - should not happen)
    warning("Block ", block_id, ": training-end filter failed, using diffuse prior")
    theta_hat$att_train_end <- c(0, 0)
    theta_hat$Ptt_train_end <- diag(1e6, 2)
    theta_hat$at_trade_start <- c(0, 0)
    theta_hat$Pt_trade_start <- diag(1e6, 2)
    theta_hat$sigma_chi_emp <- NA_real_
  }

  message("  [Block ", block_id, "] MLE done — logLik = ",
          round(theta_hat$loglik_converged, 2),
          "  (", length(valid), "/", n_starts, " runs valid)")
  message("  [Block ", block_id, "] kappa = ",   round(theta_hat$kappa,     3),
          "  sigma_chi = ", round(theta_hat$sigma_chi, 3),
          "  sigma_xi = ",  round(theta_hat$sigma_xi,  3),
          "  rho = ",       round(theta_hat$rho,       3))
  message("  [Block ", block_id, "] Training-end state: chi = ",
          round(theta_hat$att_train_end[1], 4),
          "  xi = ", round(theta_hat$att_train_end[2], 4))
  message("  [Block ", block_id, "] First-trade-week prior: chi = ",
          round(theta_hat$at_trade_start[1], 4),
          "  xi = ", round(theta_hat$at_trade_start[2], 4))

  theta_hat
}

```


## Step 4: Forward Kalman Filter Function
This section defines run_forward_kf(), which takes a fixed theta_hat
from Step 3 and runs the Kalman filter forward over one trading year. It
extracts the filtered chi and xi paths used to construct the trading
signal in Step 5, and returns the final filtered state and covariance to
be carried forward as the prior for the next trading year.

```{r step4, message=TRUE, warning=FALSE}

#############################################################################
# STEP 4.0 — run_forward_kf(): forward Kalman filter for one trading year
#
# Arguments:
#   theta_hat  : parameter list returned by estimate_ss() (Step 3)
#   Y_trade    : 5 x n_trade log-price matrix for the trading window
#   Tau_trade  : 5 x n_trade maturity matrix for the trading window
#   Delta_t    : weekly time step in years (= DELTA_T from Step 0)
#   m0_init    : 2x1 one-step-ahead prior mean for the first trading week,
#                  obtained from at[, n_train + 1] under this year's theta.
#   P0_init    : 2x2 one-step-ahead prior covariance for the first trading week,
#                  obtained from Pt[,, n_train + 1] under this year's theta.
#   block_id   : integer label used in messages only
#
# Returns a list:
#   $chi_vec    : numeric vector length n_trade; filtered chi at each week
#                 = fkf$att[1, ]; posterior mean of chi given all data up to t
#   $xi_vec     : numeric vector length n_trade; filtered xi at each week
#                 = fkf$att[2, ]
#   $att_last   : numeric 2x1; filtered state at final week of trading year
#   $Ptt_last   : numeric 2x2; filtered covariance at final week of trading year
#   $kf         : the full fkf object (stored for diagnostics)
#
# Critical look-ahead bias note:
#   att[, t] is the POSTERIOR mean E[x_t | y_1,...,y_t], it uses week t data
#   but nothing from week t+1 onwards.
#############################################################################

run_forward_kf <- function(theta_hat, Y_trade, Tau_trade, Delta_t,
                           m0_init, P0_init, block_id) {

  stopifnot(ncol(Y_trade) == ncol(Tau_trade))
  stopifnot(length(m0_init) == 2L)
  stopifnot(all(dim(P0_init) == c(2L, 2L)))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(m0_init)))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(P0_init)))

  n_trade <- ncol(Y_trade)

  # ── 1. Build state-space arrays from fixed theta_hat ──────────────────────
  # Uses the exact same make_ss_arrays() as the estimation code.
  # Parameters are FIXED at theta_hat, no re-estimation here.
  ss <- make_ss_arrays(theta_hat, Tau_trade, Delta_t)

  if (any(!is.finite(ss$ct))) {
    stop("Block ", block_id, ": make_ss_arrays() produced non-finite ct. ",
         "Check theta_hat validity.")
  }

  # ── 2. Apply missing data mask ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Identical procedure to estimation code, missing contracts are neutralised
  # in the measurement equation and their variance is inflated to near-infinity.
  masked <- apply_missing_mask_fkf(Y_trade, ss)

  # ── 3. Run Kalman filter with the correctly timed predictive prior ─────────
  # FKF updates the first supplied observation before applying its next state
  # transition. Therefore a0/P0 must already describe the first trading-week
  # state. The caller supplies at[, n_train + 1] / Pt[,, n_train + 1] from a
  # clean training-sample refilter under the current annual theta.
  kf <- tryCatch(
    fkf(
      a0  = m0_init,   P0  = P0_init,    # prior mean and covariance
      dt  = masked$dt, ct  = masked$ct,  # state drift + measurement intercept
      Tt  = masked$Tt, Zt  = masked$Zt,  # transition + measurement matrices
      HHt = masked$HHt, GGt = masked$GGt,# process noise + measurement noise
      yt  = masked$yt                    # observations (NAs replaced + masked)
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      stop("Block ", block_id, ": fkf() failed during forward filter. ",
           "Error: ", conditionMessage(e))
    }
  )

  if (any(kf$status != 0L)) {
    warning("Block ", block_id,
            ": FKF LAPACK failure status: ", paste(kf$status, collapse = ", "),
            ". Results may be unreliable for this trading year.")
  }

  # ── 4. Extract filtered state paths ───────────────────────────────────────
  # fkf$att is the 2 x n_trade matrix of POSTERIOR filtered means.
  # att[1, t] = E[chi_t | y_1,...,y_t]; short-term factor at week t
  # att[2, t] = E[xi_t  | y_1,...,y_t]; long-term factor at week t
  # This is what we use for the signal; posterior, not prior.
  chi_vec <- as.numeric(kf$att[1L, ])   # length n_trade
  xi_vec  <- as.numeric(kf$att[2L, ])   # length n_trade

  stopifnot(length(chi_vec) == n_trade)
  stopifnot(length(xi_vec)  == n_trade)

  # ── 5. Extract final state and covariance for diagnostics ─────────────────
  # att[, n_trade]   = filtered state at the last week of this trading year
  # Ptt[,, n_trade]  = filtered covariance at the last week of this trading year
  att_last <- as.numeric(kf$att[, n_trade])     # length 2
  Ptt_last <- kf$Ptt[, , n_trade]               # 2 x 2 matrix

  stopifnot(length(att_last) == 2L)
  stopifnot(all(dim(Ptt_last) == c(2L, 2L)))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(att_last)))

  list(
    chi_vec  = chi_vec,
    xi_vec   = xi_vec,
    att_last = att_last,
    Ptt_last = Ptt_last,
    kf       = kf
  )
}

```


## Step 5: Annual Expanding-Window Estimation and Filtering
This step is the model-estimation backbone shared with the relative-value strategy,
but it produces only the annual parameter estimates and filtered latent states
needed by the directional strategies. No calendar spread is constructed and no
directional P&L is calculated here.

For trading year \(y\), the model is estimated using observations from
1990 through the final observation of year \(y-1\). The fitted parameters are
then held fixed throughout year \(y\). The Kalman filter is forward-only:
the posterior state at date \(t\) uses observations through \(t\), never
future observations or smoothed states.

The explicit cache is accepted only when the input files, this
notebook, the sample dates, and the estimation settings have identical
fingerprints. Deleting the cache simply forces a full rebuild.

```{r annual-expanding-estimation, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}

MODEL_CACHE_VERSION <- "directional-final-v1-2026-10-12"
MODEL_CACHE <- file.path(PATH_OUTPUT, "ss2000_annual_model_cache.rds")

safe_md5 <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NA_character_)
  unname(tools::md5sum(path))
}

cache_signature <- list(
  version = MODEL_CACHE_VERSION,
  notebook_md5 = if (has_input_file) safe_md5(input_file) else NA_character_,
  futures_md5 = safe_md5(PATH_FUTURES),
  tbill_md5 = safe_md5(PATH_TBILL),
  train_start = as.character(TRAIN_START),
  first_trade = as.character(FIRST_TRADE),
  final_observation = as.character(max(obs_dates)),
  delta_t = DELTA_T,
  n_starts = N_STARTS,
  contracts = CONTRACTS,
  dev_mode = DEV_MODE,
  dev_end = as.character(DEV_END)
)

use_model_cache <- FALSE
if (file.exists(MODEL_CACHE)) {
  cached_model <- tryCatch(readRDS(MODEL_CACHE), error = function(e) NULL)
  use_model_cache <- is.list(cached_model) &&
    all(c("signature", "results_df", "theta_list", "schedule") %in%
          names(cached_model)) &&
    identical(cached_model$signature, cache_signature)
}

if (use_model_cache) {
  results_df <- cached_model$results_df
  theta_list <- cached_model$theta_list
  schedule <- cached_model$schedule
  message("Using validated annual-model cache: ", MODEL_CACHE)
} else {
  n_blocks <- nrow(schedule)
  state_results <- vector("list", n_blocks)
  theta_list <- vector("list", n_blocks)

  message("Starting annual expanding-window estimation: ", n_blocks,
          " trading years")

  for (k in seq_len(n_blocks)) {
    blk <- schedule[k, ]
    train_idx <- blk$train_start_idx:blk$train_end_idx
    trade_idx <- blk$trade_start_idx:blk$trade_end_idx

    theta_hat_k <- estimate_ss(
      Y_train = Y[, train_idx, drop = FALSE],
      Tau_train = Tau[, train_idx, drop = FALSE],
      Delta_t = DELTA_T,
      n_starts = N_STARTS,
      block_id = k
    )
    theta_list[[k]] <- theta_hat_k

    kf_k <- run_forward_kf(
      theta_hat = theta_hat_k,
      Y_trade = Y[, trade_idx, drop = FALSE],
      Tau_trade = Tau[, trade_idx, drop = FALSE],
      Delta_t = DELTA_T,
      m0_init = theta_hat_k$at_trade_start,
      P0_init = theta_hat_k$Pt_trade_start,
      block_id = k
    )

    rate_annual_pct <- dtb3[trade_idx]
    rate_weekly <- ifelse(
      is.finite(rate_annual_pct) & rate_annual_pct > 0,
      (1 + rate_annual_pct / 100)^(7 / 365.25) - 1,
      0
    )

    state_results[[k]] <- data.frame(
      date = obs_dates[trade_idx],
      trading_year = blk$trading_year,
      chi = kf_k$chi_vec,
      xi = kf_k$xi_vec,
      tbill_rate_weekly = rate_weekly,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    message("  Completed trading year ", blk$trading_year,
            " using data through ", obs_dates[blk$train_end_idx])
  }

  results_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(state_results)
  names(theta_list) <- as.character(schedule$trading_year)

  stopifnot(nrow(results_df) == sum(schedule$n_trade_weeks))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(results_df$chi)))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(results_df$xi)))
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(results_df$tbill_rate_weekly)))
  stopifnot(all(schedule$train_end_idx < schedule$trade_start_idx))

  saveRDS(
    list(
      signature = cache_signature,
      results_df = results_df,
      theta_list = theta_list,
      schedule = schedule
    ),
    MODEL_CACHE
  )
}

if (is.null(names(theta_list))) {
  names(theta_list) <- as.character(schedule$trading_year)
}

stopifnot(
  nrow(results_df) == sum(schedule$n_trade_weeks),
  all(as.Date(results_df$date) >= FIRST_TRADE),
  all(is.finite(results_df$chi)),
  all(is.finite(results_df$xi)),
  all(schedule$train_end_idx < schedule$trade_start_idx)
)

```


## Step 6: Frozen Directional Research Design
The hypotheses, trading universe, sample split, costs, and margin conventions
are declared before the calibration exercise. The model-estimation panel is
common to both strategies, but every backtest below holds only one outright
futures maturity at a time.

```{r directional-design, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

CALIBRATION_END <- as.Date("2016-12-31")
OOS_START       <- as.Date("2017-01-01")

DIRECTIONAL_INITIAL_CAPITAL <- 1e6
DIRECTIONAL_CONTRACT_SIZE   <- 1000L
DIRECTIONAL_COST_PER_SIDE   <- 12.50

# Maturity-specific outright margins. Construction follows the relative-value
# methodology: conservative maintenance rounding, 110% HRP initial margin
# rounded to the next $250, a 2x initial stress, and no arbitrary contract or
# gross-notional ceiling. The last column is a robustness stress only.
DIRECTIONAL_MARGIN_SCHEDULE <- data.frame(
  contract_rank = c(1L, 2L, 3L, 5L, 9L, 13L, 17L),
  cme_reference_date = as.Date("2025-12-26"),
  cme_reference_long = c(4225, 4132, 3924, 3746, 3383, 3110, 2794),
  cme_reference_short = c(3732, 3547, 3314, 3135, 2776, 2494, 2258),
  maintenance = c(4250, 4250, 4000, 3750, 3500, 3250, 3000),
  initial = c(4750, 4750, 4500, 4250, 4000, 3750, 3500),
  stress_primary = c(9500, 9500, 9000, 8500, 8000, 7500, 7000),
  historical_reference_date = as.Date("2022-03-21"),
  historical_exchange_margin = c(12000, 10500, 9500, 7800, 6800, 6400, 5900),
  stress_historical = c(13250, 11750, 10500, 8750, 8000, 7500, 7000),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
DIRECTIONAL_MAX_STRESS_MARGIN_UTILIZATION <- 0.80
DIRECTIONAL_TBILL_HAIRCUT <- 0.005

directional_margin_terms <- function(contract_rank,
                                     margin_scenario = c("primary", "historical")) {
  margin_scenario <- match.arg(margin_scenario)
  row <- DIRECTIONAL_MARGIN_SCHEDULE[
    DIRECTIONAL_MARGIN_SCHEDULE$contract_rank == as.integer(contract_rank),
    , drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(row) != 1L) stop("No outright-margin terms for CL", contract_rank)
  list(
    maintenance = row$maintenance,
    initial = row$initial,
    stress = if (margin_scenario == "primary") row$stress_primary else
      row$stress_historical,
    scenario = margin_scenario
  )
}

PRIMARY_CONTRACT_RANK <- 1L
ROBUSTNESS_CONTRACT_RANKS <- c(2L, 3L)

directional_design <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Model estimation panel", "Initial estimation", "Parameter updates",
    "Trading sample", "Calibration/development", "Retrospective OOS",
    "Contrarian signal", "Model-forecast signal", "Primary traded contract",
    "Position size", "Base cost", "Outright margin", "Roll execution"
  ),
  Choice = c(
    "CL1, CL5, CL9, CL13 and CL17",
    "1990-1999",
    "Annual expanding window",
    "2000-2025",
    "2000-2016",
    "2017-2025",
    "position = -sign(filtered chi)",
    "position = sign(one-week SS2000 log-price forecast change)",
    "CL1",
    "One contract",
    "$12.50 per one-way contract-side",
    "Maturity-specific; 2x initial stress, 80% equity limit",
    "Actual underlying ticker with LTD-safe pre-roll"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  directional_design,
  caption = "Frozen directional research design",
  align = c("l", "l")
)

```


## Step 7: Decision States and Executable Contract Paths
The decision state for a weekly return interval is the filtered posterior
available at the preceding weekly close. At the first observation of each
calendar year, the relevant decision is the final December posterior produced
by that year's newly estimated expanding-window model.

```{r directional-reference, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

directional_ref <- as.data.frame(results_df)
directional_ref$date <- as.Date(directional_ref$date)

trade_rows <- match(directional_ref$date, obs_dates)
if (anyNA(trade_rows)) stop("Directional dates do not align with obs_dates")

theta_by_year <- stats::setNames(theta_list, schedule$trading_year)

is_year_start <- c(TRUE, diff(directional_ref$trading_year) != 0)
decision_chi <- decision_xi <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(directional_ref))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(directional_ref))) {
  yr <- as.character(directional_ref$trading_year[i])
  th <- theta_by_year[[yr]]
  if (is.null(th)) stop("Missing annual theta for year ", yr)

  if (is_year_start[i]) {
    decision_chi[i] <- th$att_train_end[1L]
    decision_xi[i]  <- th$att_train_end[2L]
  } else {
    decision_chi[i] <- directional_ref$chi[i - 1L]
    decision_xi[i]  <- directional_ref$xi[i - 1L]
  }
}

if (any(!is.finite(decision_chi)) || any(!is.finite(decision_xi))) {
  stop("Decision states contain invalid values")
}

# Construct a single-leg executable path using helper functions and
# timing convention. Each weekly change is measured on
# one actual exchange ticker; generic-series jumps never enter P&L.
build_single_leg_execution <- function(contract_rank) {
  stopifnot(length(contract_rank) == 1L, contract_rank >= 1L,
            contract_rank <= ncol(UND_ALL))

  n <- nrow(directional_ref)
  target_ticker <- rep(NA_character_, n)
  price_prev <- price_curr <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  ltd_curr <- as.Date(rep(NA_real_, n), origin = "1970-01-01")
  exec_roll <- logical(n)

  held_ticker <- NA_character_

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    idx_now  <- trade_rows[i]
    idx_prev <- idx_now - 1L
    if (idx_prev < 1L) stop("No prior observation for directional execution")

    row_prev_px  <- PX_ALL[idx_prev,  , drop = TRUE]
    row_prev_und <- UND_ALL[idx_prev, , drop = TRUE]
    row_prev_ltd <- LTD_ALL[idx_prev, , drop = TRUE]
    row_curr_px  <- PX_ALL[idx_now,   , drop = TRUE]
    row_curr_und <- UND_ALL[idx_now,  , drop = TRUE]
    row_curr_ltd <- LTD_ALL[idx_now,  , drop = TRUE]

    generic_next <- UND_ALL[idx_now, contract_rank]
    previous_ticker <- held_ticker

    held_ticker <- choose_execution_ticker(
      held_ticker         = held_ticker,
      generic_ticker_next = generic_next,
      prev_und_row        = row_prev_und,
      prev_ltd_row        = row_prev_ltd,
      next_obs_date       = directional_ref$date[i]
    )

    px0 <- lookup_ticker_price(row_prev_px, row_prev_und, held_ticker)
    px1 <- lookup_ticker_price(row_curr_px, row_curr_und, held_ticker)
    ltd <- lookup_ticker_ltd(row_curr_ltd, row_curr_und, held_ticker)

    if (!is.finite(px0) || !is.finite(px1) || px0 <= 0 || px1 <= 0) {
      stop("Invalid executable price for ", held_ticker, " on ",
           directional_ref$date[i])
    }

    target_ticker[i] <- held_ticker
    price_prev[i] <- px0
    price_curr[i] <- px1
    ltd_curr[i] <- ltd
    exec_roll[i] <- i > 1L && !is.na(previous_ticker) &&
      previous_ticker != held_ticker
  }

  data.frame(
    date = directional_ref$date,
    contract_rank = contract_rank,
    target_ticker = target_ticker,
    price_prev = price_prev,
    price_curr = price_curr,
    ltd_curr = ltd_curr,
    exec_roll = exec_roll,
    unit_long_gross = (price_curr - price_prev) * DIRECTIONAL_CONTRACT_SIZE,
    realized_log_change = log(price_curr / price_prev),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

execution_CL1 <- build_single_leg_execution(1L)

```


## Step 8: Directional Signal Definitions
The **Short-Term-Deviation Contrarian Strategy** tests the direct mapping from
the filtered short-term deviation to the opposite outright position. The
**One-Week Model-Forecast Strategy** propagates both latent factors one week
under the physical transition equation and reprices the actual held contract
at its next-week maturity. The forecast is a conditional mean of log price: it
never uses the realized next-week price.

```{r directional-signals, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

fill_zero_signal <- function(x) {
  x <- as.integer(sign(x))
  for (i in seq_along(x)) {
    if (x[i] == 0L && i > 1L) x[i] <- x[i - 1L]
  }
  x
}

position_deviation <- fill_zero_signal(-decision_chi)

forecast_log_price  <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(directional_ref))
forecast_log_change <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(directional_ref))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(directional_ref))) {
  yr <- as.character(directional_ref$trading_year[i])
  th <- theta_by_year[[yr]]

  chi_next <- exp(-th$kappa * DELTA_T) * decision_chi[i]
  xi_next  <- decision_xi[i] + th$mu * DELTA_T

  tau_next <- as.numeric(execution_CL1$ltd_curr[i] - directional_ref$date[i]) /
    365.25
  tau_next <- max(tau_next, 0)

  forecast_log_price[i] <-
    exp(-th$kappa * tau_next) * chi_next + xi_next +
    A_fun(
      tau_next, th$kappa, th$mu_star, th$sigma_chi,
      th$sigma_xi, th$rho, th$lambda_chi
    )

  forecast_log_change[i] <-
    forecast_log_price[i] - log(execution_CL1$price_prev[i])
}

if (any(!is.finite(forecast_log_change))) {
  stop("The one-week model-forecast signal contains invalid values")
}

position_forecast <- fill_zero_signal(forecast_log_change)

signal_frame <- data.frame(
  date = directional_ref$date,
  trading_year = directional_ref$trading_year,
  decision_chi = decision_chi,
  decision_xi = decision_xi,
  position_deviation = position_deviation,
  forecast_log_price = forecast_log_price,
  forecast_log_change = forecast_log_change,
  position_forecast = position_forecast,
  realized_log_change = execution_CL1$realized_log_change,
  signals_agree = position_deviation == position_forecast
)

signal_diagnostics <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Weeks", "Signal agreement", "Contrarian long share",
    "Contrarian short share", "Model-forecast long share",
    "Model-forecast short share", "CL1 execution rolls"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(signal_frame),
    mean(signal_frame$signals_agree),
    mean(signal_frame$position_deviation == 1L),
    mean(signal_frame$position_deviation == -1L),
    mean(signal_frame$position_forecast == 1L),
    mean(signal_frame$position_forecast == -1L),
    sum(execution_CL1$exec_roll)
  )
)

knitr::kable(signal_diagnostics, digits = 4,
             caption = "Pre-specified signal diagnostics")

```


## Step 9: One-Contract Baseline P&L
The simulator requests exactly one contract when active and then checks that
position against the maturity-specific stressed-margin capacity. Costs are
charged for entries, exits, reversals, rolls and terminal liquidation. A roll
plus a reversal requires closing the old ticker and opening the new ticker,
which is two contract-sides rather than four.

```{r directional-pnl-engine, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

simulate_directional <- function(execution, position, strategy_id,
                                 cost_per_side = DIRECTIONAL_COST_PER_SIDE,
                                 initial_capital = DIRECTIONAL_INITIAL_CAPITAL,
                                 margin_scenario = c("primary", "historical")) {
  margin_scenario <- match.arg(margin_scenario)
  n <- nrow(execution)
  stopifnot(length(position) == n)
  stopifnot(all(position %in% c(-1L, 0L, 1L)))
  stopifnot(cost_per_side >= 0)
  rank <- unique(execution$contract_rank)
  if (length(rank) != 1L) stop("Each directional simulation must use one maturity")
  margin <- directional_margin_terms(rank, margin_scenario)

  gross <- costs <- net <- tbill_pnl <- total_pnl <- capital <- numeric(n)
  capital_start_week <- numeric(n)
  margin_posted <- maintenance_required <- stress_required <- numeric(n)
  stress_limit <- stress_util_start <- stress_util_end <- numeric(n)
  margin_face_value <- idle_cash <- numeric(n)
  contracts <- margin_capacity <- integer(n)
  signed_quantity <- integer(n)
  margin_cap_binding <- maintenance_margin_call <- logical(n)
  contract_sides <- integer(n)
  trade_event <- rep("none", n)
  roll_event <- logical(n)
  capital_running <- initial_capital

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    pos_now  <- position[i]
    q_prev <- if (i == 1L) 0L else signed_quantity[i - 1L]
    ticker_now  <- execution$target_ticker[i]
    ticker_prev <- if (i == 1L) NA_character_ else execution$target_ticker[i - 1L]
    ticker_changed <- i > 1L && !is.na(ticker_prev) && ticker_prev != ticker_now
    capital_start_week[i] <- capital_running

    margin_capacity[i] <- max(0L, as.integer(floor(
      DIRECTIONAL_MAX_STRESS_MARGIN_UTILIZATION * max(capital_running, 0) /
        margin$stress
    )))
    desired_contracts <- abs(pos_now)
    contracts[i] <- min(desired_contracts, margin_capacity[i])
    margin_cap_binding[i] <- desired_contracts > margin_capacity[i]
    q_now <- pos_now * contracts[i]
    signed_quantity[i] <- q_now

    sides_i <- if (ticker_changed && (q_prev != 0L || q_now != 0L)) {
      abs(q_prev) + abs(q_now)
    } else {
      abs(q_now - q_prev)
    }

    # Charge terminal liquidation after the final weekly P&L.
    if (i == n && q_now != 0L) sides_i <- sides_i + abs(q_now)

    event_i <- dplyr::case_when(
      q_prev == 0L && q_now != 0L ~ "entry",
      q_prev != 0L && q_now == 0L ~ "exit",
      q_prev * q_now < 0L && ticker_changed ~ "roll_and_reversal",
      q_prev * q_now < 0L ~ "reversal",
      ticker_changed && q_now != 0L ~ "roll",
      TRUE ~ "none"
    )
    if (i == n && q_now != 0L) {
      event_i <- if (event_i == "none") "terminal_liquidation" else
        paste0(event_i, "+terminal_liquidation")
    }

    gross[i] <- q_now * execution$unit_long_gross[i]
    costs[i] <- sides_i * cost_per_side
    net[i] <- gross[i] - costs[i]

    margin_posted[i] <- margin$initial * contracts[i]
    maintenance_required[i] <- margin$maintenance * contracts[i]
    stress_required[i] <- margin$stress * contracts[i]
    stress_limit[i] <- DIRECTIONAL_MAX_STRESS_MARGIN_UTILIZATION * capital_running
    stress_util_start[i] <- if (capital_running > 0) {
      stress_required[i] / capital_running
    } else if (stress_required[i] > 0) Inf else 0
    margin_face_value[i] <- margin_posted[i] / (1 - DIRECTIONAL_TBILL_HAIRCUT)
    idle_cash[i] <- capital_running - margin_posted[i]
    if (idle_cash[i] < -1e-8 || stress_required[i] > stress_limit[i] + 1e-8) {
      stop("Directional margin invariant failed on ", execution$date[i])
    }

    # As in the RV account, only cash not posted as margin earns DTB3.
    weekly_rate <- directional_ref$tbill_rate_weekly[i]
    if (!is.finite(weekly_rate)) weekly_rate <- 0
    tbill_pnl[i] <- idle_cash[i] * weekly_rate
    total_pnl[i] <- net[i] + tbill_pnl[i]
    capital_running <- capital_running + total_pnl[i]
    capital[i] <- capital_running
    maintenance_margin_call[i] <- contracts[i] > 0L &&
      capital_running < maintenance_required[i]
    stress_util_end[i] <- if (capital_running > 0) {
      stress_required[i] / capital_running
    } else if (stress_required[i] > 0) Inf else 0

    contract_sides[i] <- sides_i
    trade_event[i] <- event_i
    roll_event[i] <- ticker_changed && q_now != 0L && q_prev != 0L
  }

  data.frame(
    strategy_id = strategy_id,
    date = execution$date,
    trading_year = directional_ref$trading_year,
    target_ticker = execution$target_ticker,
    price_prev = execution$price_prev,
    price_curr = execution$price_curr,
    position = position,
    contracts = contracts,
    signed_quantity = signed_quantity,
    unit_long_gross = execution$unit_long_gross,
    gross_futures_pnl = gross,
    contract_sides_traded = contract_sides,
    transaction_cost = costs,
    net_futures_pnl = net,
    margin_scenario = margin_scenario,
    margin_per_contract_initial = margin$initial,
    margin_per_contract_maintenance = margin$maintenance,
    margin_per_contract_stress = margin$stress,
    margin_posted = margin_posted,
    maintenance_margin_required = maintenance_required,
    stress_margin_required = stress_required,
    stress_margin_limit = stress_limit,
    stress_margin_utilization_start = stress_util_start,
    stress_margin_utilization_end = stress_util_end,
    margin_face_value = margin_face_value,
    idle_cash = idle_cash,
    margin_capacity_contracts = margin_capacity,
    margin_cap_binding = margin_cap_binding,
    maintenance_margin_call = maintenance_margin_call,
    capital_start_week = capital_start_week,
    tbill_rate_weekly = directional_ref$tbill_rate_weekly,
    tbill_pnl = tbill_pnl,
    total_pnl = total_pnl,
    capital = capital,
    exec_roll = roll_event,
    trade_event = trade_event,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

weekly_deviation <- simulate_directional(execution_CL1, position_deviation, "DEV_CONTRARIAN_CL1")
weekly_forecast <- simulate_directional(execution_CL1, position_forecast, "MODEL_FORECAST_CL1")
weekly_long <- simulate_directional(
  execution_CL1, rep(1L, nrow(directional_ref)), "Always_Long"
)
weekly_short <- simulate_directional(
  execution_CL1, rep(-1L, nrow(directional_ref)), "Always_Short"
)

# Attach the decision variables needed for transparent weekly exports.
weekly_deviation$decision_chi <- decision_chi
weekly_deviation$decision_xi <- decision_xi
weekly_deviation$forecast_log_change <- forecast_log_change
weekly_deviation$realized_log_change <- execution_CL1$realized_log_change

weekly_forecast$decision_chi <- decision_chi
weekly_forecast$decision_xi <- decision_xi
weekly_forecast$forecast_log_change <- forecast_log_change
weekly_forecast$realized_log_change <- execution_CL1$realized_log_change

```


## Step 10: Baseline Performance and Predictive Evidence
Futures performance is evaluated separately from passive T-bill income. The
information ratio uses weekly net futures P&L divided by start-of-week account
equity, while drawdown uses the net-futures equity path. Collateral returns
therefore cannot mask a weak trading signal.

```{r directional-summaries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

period_definitions <- data.frame(
  period = c(
    "Calibration 2000-2016",
    "Retrospective OOS 2017-2025",
    "Full 2000-2025"
  ),
  start = as.Date(c("2000-01-01", "2017-01-01", "2000-01-01")),
  end = as.Date(c("2016-12-31", "2025-12-31", "2025-12-31"))
)

max_futures_drawdown_pct <- function(pnl, base_capital) {
  wealth <- base_capital + cumsum(pnl)
  peak <- cummax(c(base_capital, wealth))[-1L]
  min((wealth - peak) / peak) * 100
}

summarize_directional_period <- function(x, period_name, start_date, end_date) {
  y <- x[x$date >= start_date & x$date <= end_date, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(y) == 0L) stop("Empty period: ", period_name)

  weekly_futures_return <- y$net_futures_pnl / y$capital_start_week
  return_sd <- stats::sd(weekly_futures_return)
  info_ratio <- if (is.finite(return_sd) && return_sd > 0) {
    sqrt(52) * mean(weekly_futures_return) / return_sd
  } else NA_real_

  starts <- c(TRUE, y$position[-1L] != y$position[-nrow(y)])

  data.frame(
    strategy_id = unique(y$strategy_id),
    period = period_name,
    start_date = min(y$date),
    end_date = max(y$date),
    weeks = nrow(y),
    gross_futures_pnl = sum(y$gross_futures_pnl),
    transaction_cost = sum(y$transaction_cost),
    net_futures_pnl = sum(y$net_futures_pnl),
    information_ratio = info_ratio,
    max_futures_drawdown_pct = max_futures_drawdown_pct(
      y$net_futures_pnl, y$capital_start_week[1L]
    ),
    long_weeks = sum(y$position == 1L),
    short_weeks = sum(y$position == -1L),
    flat_weeks = sum(y$position == 0L),
    position_episodes = sum(starts & y$position != 0L),
    contract_sides_traded = sum(y$contract_sides_traded),
    roll_weeks = sum(y$exec_roll),
    tbill_pnl = sum(y$tbill_pnl),
    ending_capital = tail(y$capital, 1L),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

# Newey-West/HAC covariance for a compact predictive regression. Lag four is
# fixed in advance and is not selected from the result.
fit_hac_regression <- function(y, x, lag = 4L, label = "Full") {
  keep <- is.finite(y) & is.finite(x)
  y <- as.numeric(y[keep])
  x <- as.numeric(x[keep])
  X <- cbind(`(Intercept)` = 1, decision_chi = x)
  n <- nrow(X)
  k <- ncol(X)
  beta <- solve(crossprod(X), crossprod(X, y))
  u <- as.numeric(y - X %*% beta)

  meat <- matrix(0, k, k)
  for (t in seq_len(n)) {
    xt <- matrix(X[t, ], ncol = 1)
    meat <- meat + u[t]^2 * (xt %*% t(xt))
  }
  if (lag > 0L) {
    for (ell in seq_len(lag)) {
      weight <- 1 - ell / (lag + 1)
      gamma <- matrix(0, k, k)
      for (t in (ell + 1L):n) {
        xt <- matrix(X[t, ], ncol = 1)
        xl <- matrix(X[t - ell, ], ncol = 1)
        gamma <- gamma + u[t] * u[t - ell] * (xt %*% t(xl))
      }
      meat <- meat + weight * (gamma + t(gamma))
    }
  }

  bread <- solve(crossprod(X))
  vcov_hac <- (n / (n - k)) * bread %*% meat %*% bread
  se <- sqrt(diag(vcov_hac))
  t_stat <- beta / se
  p_two_sided <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(t_stat))

  data.frame(
    period = label,
    observations = n,
    intercept = beta[1L],
    intercept_hac_se = se[1L],
    beta_chi = beta[2L],
    beta_chi_hac_se = se[2L],
    beta_chi_t = t_stat[2L],
    beta_chi_p_two_sided = p_two_sided[2L],
    hac_lag = lag
  )
}

predictive_regression <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(period_definitions)), function(i) {
  use <- signal_frame$date >= period_definitions$start[i] &
    signal_frame$date <= period_definitions$end[i]
  fit_hac_regression(
    signal_frame$realized_log_change[use],
    signal_frame$decision_chi[use],
    lag = 4L,
    label = period_definitions$period[i]
  )
}))
```
